sections.h2: How do Gurnee owners usually decide between a listing and a fast sale?
sections.html:
Most weigh the condition of the house against the days they can afford to wait. A move-in-ready home can justify a listing, while a house that needs work or an owner facing a deadline points toward an as-is purchase. All three routes end the same way, with a deed recorded at the Lake County Clerk.

  • Agent listing: a wider pool of buyers, balanced against inspections, repair requests and a lender's timetable.
  • Owner-handled sale: you keep the commission and take on showings, disclosures and the contract.
  • As-is cash sale: a shorter path to closing, with the buyer assuming whatever repairs remain.

Gather recent sales on your street first, because Gurnee houses are priced against their neighbors, not against the resort attractions nearby.

sections.h2: Where is Gurnee and how did it start?
sections.html:
Gurnee sits on the Des Plaines River in Lake County, roughly 40 miles north of Chicago and 50 miles south of Milwaukee, next to Waukegan. The village was founded in 1928 and carries the name of Walter S. Gurnee, a Chicago mayor who was also a railroad director. It covers a little over 13 square miles.

The first families came in the 1830s, and the crossroads was originally called Wentworth before the railroad station took the Gurnee name. A stagecoach stop on the old Milwaukee Road, known as the Mother Rudd House, now holds the Warren Township Historical Society.

Interstate 94 splits the village into an older east side and a newer west side. Pace buses link Gurnee with Waukegan and Grayslake, and a CPKC rail line between Chicago and Minneapolis runs through town.

Gurnee is a home rule municipality run by a council-manager system, with a Village President and six trustees serving four-year terms. Education levels are high: 56.7 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and 67.9 percent of residents 16 and older are in the labor force. About 17 percent of residents were born outside the country, and 26.1 percent speak a language other than English at home, which can be worth remembering when you write a listing or an offer letter.

sections.h2: Why do so many visitors come to Gurnee?
sections.html:
Gurnee is a regional destination. Six Flags Great America opened in 1976 as Marriott's Great America, and its Hurricane Harbor water park arrived in 2005. Gurnee Mills, open since 1991, ranks as the fourth largest mall in Illinois, and the Great Wolf Lodge resort opened in 2007. Together they bring about 23 million visits a year and are among the village's biggest revenue sources.

Corporate employers include High Sierra Sport Company and PurposeBuilt Brands, which owns Goo Gone. In 2022, Census data show retail sales of about $1.4 billion, or $46,148 per resident. Buyers will want to know how close a house sits to the I-94 corridor and the attraction areas, so be ready to describe its location.

Gurnee Mills has drawn between 15 million and 20 million visitors a year since it opened, and Six Flags Great America alone had about 3 million guests in 2023.

sections.html:

sections.h2: Which schools do Gurnee buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Two elementary districts share the village. Gurnee School District 56 covers most of the east half through Spaulding (pre-K to grade 2), Prairie Trail (grades 3 to 5), Viking Middle School (grades 6 to 8) and River Trail (kindergarten to grade 8).

  • Woodland District 50 covers the west side and part of the east, with Primary, Elementary, Intermediate and Middle schools.
  • Warren Township High School, District 121, serves everyone: freshmen and sophomores at the O'Plaine Road campus, juniors and seniors at Almond Road.
  • Prairie Crossing Charter School takes kindergarten through grade 8 students from Districts 50 and 79.

Look up which side of town your address falls on before you describe the house. The Warren-Newport Public Library, with more than 270,000 books and a service area of about 60,000 people, is another amenity families mention.

sections.h2: What flood history should a Gurnee seller expect questions about?
sections.html:
The May 2004 storm brought the worst flooding in a century, closed schools and damaged dozens of homes and businesses. The Village names the low ground along the Des Plaines River and its tributaries as the most dangerous flood hazard area.

  • Look up your address on the Federal Insurance Rate Map and on the Village's inundation map.
  • Basements built more recently must have a sump pump ejection system, and the Village urges backups.
  • The Engineering Division, at 847-599-7550, keeps elevation certificates supplied by owners and historical flood records.
  • The Village's participation in the Community Rating System earns policyholders a 5 to 20 percent insurance discount.

A voluntary floodplain buyout program is also listed among the Village's flooding resources, along with a mailing list for flood updates.

sections.h2: Which permits and utility steps come up before a Gurnee closing?
sections.html:
Most construction, remodeling and improvement projects need a permit before work starts, and the Village notes that permits can help prevent issues in later property sales. Fences, reroofs, siding, water heaters, furnaces, driveways and window replacements go through an online One Stop portal. Larger projects such as additions and garages use a separate application. For inspections, call the Building Division at 847-599-7550 with 24 hours' notice and your permit number.

The Village sets a maximum U-factor of 0.28 for replacement windows in residential projects, so keep the contractor's paperwork if you replaced yours. Water arrives from Lake Michigan through the Central Lake County Joint Action Water Agency. The Village website has a Start, Stop or Make Changes page for your service, which is the place to end your account near the closing date.

sections.h2: How is a Gurnee deed recorded?
sections.html:
The Lake County Clerk's recording division in Waukegan takes the deed. According to the Clerk's packet, the grantor's signature must be notarized and the page must show the buyer's address, a full legal description, the preparer, a return address and where tax bills go. A PTAX-203 declaration or a signed exemption statement is also required.

The packet names six municipalities that require a local stamp before recording: Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago. Gurnee does not appear on that list, but confirm with the Village before closing.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed in Gurnee?
faqs.a: The Lake County Clerk's recording division, in Waukegan. A notarized grantor signature, legal description and PTAX-203 or exemption statement are part of what it requires.

faqs.q: Does Gurnee have a local transfer stamp?
faqs.a: The Lake County Clerk lists six municipalities that need one, and Gurnee is not among them. A quick call to the Village confirms it for your closing.

faqs.q: Where can I check flood history for a Gurnee house?
faqs.a: Start with the Village's Engineering Division at 847-599-7550. It keeps flood maps, elevation certificates provided by owners and historical flood records.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Gurnee house in?
faqs.a: East side addresses mostly fall in District 56 and west side addresses in District 50, with all feeding Warren Township High School. Check your exact address.

faqs.q: What if my Gurnee house has work done without a permit?
faqs.a: Ask the Building Division about your permit record. The Village says permits can help prevent issues in future sales, and an as-is buyer can take the house regardless.
